cases.sentence: Место тяги было недалеко над речкой в ___.
cases.explain: «мелком осиннике» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The place fixed on for the stand-shooting was not far above a stream in a little aspen copse. On reaching the copse, Levin got out of the trap and led Oblonsky to a corner of a mossy, swampy glade, already quite free from snow. He went back himself to a double birch tree on the other side, and leaning his gun on the fork of a dead lower branch, he took off his full overcoat, fastened his belt again, and worked his arms to see if they were free.

cases.sentence: Сам он вернулся на ___ к двойняшке-березе и, прислонив ружье к развилине сухого нижнего сучка, снял кафтан, перепоясался и попробовал свободы движений рук.
cases.explain: «другой край» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: Солнце спускалось за ___; и на свете зари березки, рассыпанные по осиннику, отчетливо рисовались своими висящими ветвями с надутыми, готовыми лопнуть почками.
cases.explain: «крупный лес» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Gray old Laska, who had followed them, sat down warily opposite him and pricked up her ears. The sun was setting behind a thick forest, and in the glow of sunset the birch trees, dotted about in the aspen copse, stood out clearly with their hanging twigs, and their buds swollen almost to bursting.

cases.sentence: ___ щебетали и изредка пролетали с дерева на дерево.
cases.explain: «Мелкие птицы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: From the thickest parts of the copse, where the snow still remained, came the faint sound of narrow winding threads of water running away. Tiny birds twittered, and now and then fluttered from tree to tree.

cases.sentence: В промежутках ___ слышен был шорох прошлогодних листьев, шевелившихся от таянья земли и от росту трав.
cases.explain: «совершенной тишины» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: In the pauses of complete stillness there came the rustle of last year’s leaves, stirred by the thawing of the earth and the growth of the grass.

cases.sentence: Слышно и видно, как трава растет!» – сказал себе Левин, заметив двинувшийся ___ мокрый осиновый лист подле иглы молодой травы.
cases.explain: «грифельного цвета» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Imagine! One can hear and see the grass growing!” Levin said to himself, noticing a wet, slate-colored aspen leaf moving beside a blade of young grass. He stood, listened, and gazed sometimes down at the wet mossy ground, sometimes at Laska listening all alert, sometimes at the sea of bare tree tops that stretched on the slope below him, sometimes at the darkening sky, covered with white streaks of cloud. A hawk flew high over a forest far away with slow sweep of its wings; another flew with exactly the same motion in the same direction and vanished. The birds twittered more and more loudly and busily in the thicket. An owl hooted not far off, and Laska, starting, stepped cautiously a few steps forward, and putting her head on one side, began to listen intently. Beyond the stream was heard the cuckoo. Twice she uttered her usual cuckoo call, and then gave a hoarse, hurried call and broke down.

cases.sentence: Он стоял, слушал и глядел вниз, то на мокрую мшистую землю, то на прислушивающуюся Ласку, то на расстилавшееся пред ним под горою море оголенных макуш леса, то на подернутое ___ туч тускневшее небо.
cases.explain: «белыми полосками» — after the preposition «на», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.sentence: Послышался дальний, ___ и, ровно в тот обычный такт, столь знакомый охотнику, чрез две секунды, – другой, третий, и за третьим свистком уже слышно стало хорканье.
cases.explain: «тонкий свисток» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: They heard a shrill whistle in the distance, and in the exact time, so well known to the sportsman, two seconds later—another, a third, and after the third whistle the hoarse, guttural cry could be heard.
